animals.name: Otters
animals.description: A corridor of 5+ blooms, with 4+ of them touching wetland.
animals.note: Playful and shy; follows chains of wet ground and fishes at dusk.

animals.name: Deer
animals.description: A long corridor of 8+ blooms, with 6+ of them touching forest.
animals.note: Roe deer browse at the woodland edge and travel far along green corridors.

animals.name: Badgers
animals.description: A corridor of 4+ blooms, with 2+ of them Deep Woods.
animals.note: Digs its sett in the deepest woods and trundles out at night.

animals.name: Red grouse
animals.riddle: A red-browed bird calls go-back, go-back where the heather runs wide and unbroken.
animals.found_text: 6+ heath hexes joined in one patch.
animals.note: Bursts from the heather with a whirr and a call that sounds like go-back, go-back.

animals.name: Grey heron
animals.riddle: A grey shadow stands still where the reeds wade into the mere.
animals.note: Stands so still at the water's edge that fish forget it's there.

animals.name: Bees
animals.description: A corridor of 5+ blooms, with 2+ of them Foxglove Glades.
animals.note: Wild bees work the foxgloves from dawn and need flowers all along their way.

animals.name: Brown hare
animals.riddle: Long ears listen where the meadow lies broad and open, field upon field.
animals.found_text: 10+ meadow hexes joined in one patch.
animals.note: Lives out in open fields and boxes in spring; it needs room to run.

animals.name: Golden eagles
animals.description: A corridor of 5+ blooms, with 2+ of them by the cliff.
animals.note: Rides the updraughts along the crag and nests on its highest ledge.

animals.name: Wildcat
animals.riddle: A striped shadow with a ringed tail hunts where the woods climb to the rock.
animals.note: Britain's rarest cat: shy, thick-tailed and fond of wooded crags.
